verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः |
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः |
यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
yatte'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; bhūyaḥ eva—again further; mahā-bāho—O mighty-armed one (Arjuna); śṛṇu—listen; me—to My; paramam—supreme; vacaḥ—words; yat—which; te—unto you; aham—I; prīyamāṇāya—who take delight in My words; vakṣyāmi—shall speak; hita-kāmyayā—for your ultimate welfare.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Hear again, O mighty-armed one, My supreme words, which I shall speak to you who take delight in them, out of a desire for your highest spiritual welfare.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna addresses Arjuna as 'Priyamana'—one whose heart rejoices in hearing divine wisdom. Because of Arjuna's sincere devotion and eagerness, the Lord prepares to disclose even deeper revelations regarding His divine opulences (Vibhutis) and cosmic omnipresence for his eternal spiritual elevation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः |
अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः |
अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ |
ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: na—neither; me—My; viduḥ—know; sura-gaṇāḥ—the hosts of gods; prabhavam—origin/manifestation; na—nor; mahā-ṛṣayaḥ—the great sages; aham—I am; ādiḥ—the source/origin; hi—truly; devānām—of the gods; mahā-ṛṣīṇām—of the great sages; ca—and; sarvaśaḥ—in every respect.
verses.translation: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great celestial sages comprehend My divine origin, for I am in every respect the primal source of both gods and sages.
verses.meaning: Finite intellects cannot comprehend the Infinite Origin from which they themselves arose. Just as children cannot witness the birth of their own parents, neither demigods nor eminent sages can grasp the unmanifest beginning of Sri Krishna, who is the timeless fountainhead of all cosmic intelligence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् |
असंमूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् |
असंमूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yo māmajamanādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram |
asaṃmūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: yaḥ—whoever; mām—Me; ajam—unborn; anādim—without beginning; ca—and; vetti—knows; loka-mahā-īśvaram—the Supreme Sovereign of all planetary realms; asaṃmūḍhaḥ—undeluded; saḥ—he; martyeṣu—among mortals; sarva-pāpaiḥ—from all sins; pramucyate—is liberated.
verses.translation: He who knows Me as unborn (Aja), beginningless (Anadi), and the Supreme Sovereign of all the worlds (Loka-Maheshvara)—he alone among mortals is undeluded and is freed from all sins.
verses.meaning: Realizing the true transcendental nature of the Divine destroys all karmic fetters. When an individual soul realizes that Sri Krishna is not a product of material nature but the unborn, beginningless Lord of all cosmos, false ego dissolves and complete spiritual liberation is attained.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः |
सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः |
सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
buddhirjñānamasaṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ |
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayameva ca || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: buddhiḥ—intellect/discernment; jñānam—wisdom; asaṃmohaḥ—freedom from delusion; kṣamā—forgiveness/patience; satyam—truthfulness; damaḥ—control of senses; śamaḥ—peace of mind; sukham—happiness; duḥkham—sorrow; bhavaḥ—birth/existence; abhāvaḥ—death/non-existence; bhayam—fear; ca—and; abhayam—fearlessness; eva ca—and also.
verses.translation: Intellect (Buddhi), spiritual wisdom (Jnana), freedom from doubt and delusion (Asammoha), forgiveness (Kshama), truthfulness (Satya), sensory self-control (Dama), tranquility of mind (Shama), pleasure (Sukha), pain (Duhkha), birth (Bhava), death (Abhava), fear (Bhaya), and fearlessness (Abhaya);
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna enumerates the mental faculties, psychological states, and experiential dualities that govern all living entities. None of these qualities arise by random chance; they are conscious faculties originating from the Supreme Lord as part of the cosmic evolutionary setup.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः |
भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः |
भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṃ yaśo'yaśaḥ |
bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: ahiṃsā—non-violence; samatā—equanimity; tuṣṭiḥ—contentment; tapaḥ—austerity; dānam—charity; yaśaḥ—fame; ayaśaḥ—infamy; bhavanti—arise; bhāvāḥ—qualities/states of being; bhūtānām—of living beings; mattaḥ—from Me; eva—alone; pṛthak-vidhāḥ—of diverse kinds.
verses.translation: Non-violence (Ahimsa), equanimity (Samata), contentment (Tushti), austerity (Tapas), charity (Dana), fame (Yashas), and infamy (Ayashas)—all these diverse states of living beings originate from Me alone.
verses.meaning: Continuing from Verse 4, Sri Krishna affirms that all the diverse emotional and moral conditions of life—whether virtuous qualities or humbling tests—are distributed and sustained by His cosmic order according to each soul's karmic evolution.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा |
मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा |
मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā |
madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: mahā-ṛṣayaḥ sapta—the seven great sages (Bhrigu, Marichi, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vashishtha); pūrve—ancient/prior; catvāraḥ—the four (Kumaras); manavaḥ tathā—and the Manus (progenitors); mad-bhāvāḥ—born of My divine nature; mānasāḥ jātāḥ—born from the mind (of Brahma directed by Me); yeṣām—from whom; loke—in the world; imāḥ prajāḥ—all these populations/creatures.
verses.translation: The seven ancient great sages, the four primal Kumaras, and the Manus (progenitors of humanity) were all born from My mind, imbued with My divine nature, and from them all creatures in this world have descended.
verses.meaning: Cosmic genealogy: The archetypal leaders of wisdom, asceticism, and universal governance—the Saptarshis, the Four Kumaras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara), and the Manus—were projected mentally by the Supreme Will, populating and guiding the universe.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः |
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः |
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ |
so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: etām—this; vibhūtim—divine opulence/manifestation; yogam ca—and divine mystic power; mama—My; yaḥ—whoever; vetti—knows; tattvataḥ—in truth; saḥ—he; avikampena yogena—with unshakeable yoga; yujyate—becomes united; na atra saṃśayaḥ—there is no doubt about this.
verses.translation: Whoever knows in truth this divine opulence (Vibhuti) and sovereign power (Yoga) of Mine becomes united with Me in unshakeable, steadfast Yoga; of this there is no doubt.
verses.meaning: Gaining deep insight into Sri Krishna's omnipresent glory transforms intellectual belief into unshakeable, unwavering devotion (Avikampa Yoga). When one sees that every grandeur in the universe is but an expression of the Divine, the mind never deviates from constant spiritual remembrance.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते |
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते |
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate |
iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: aham—I am; sarvasya—of all creation; prabhavaḥ—the source/origin; mattaḥ—from Me; sarvam—everything; pravartate—emanates/operates; iti matvā—understanding this; bhajante—worship; mām—Me; budhāḥ—the wise; bhāva-samanvitāḥ—endowed with ecstatic loving devotion.
verses.translation: I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds; everything emanates from Me. Realizing this in truth, the wise worship Me with heartfelt, ecstatic devotion (Bhava).
verses.meaning: The first verse of the celebrated 'Chatushloki Gita' (10.8–10.11)—the four seed verses encapsulating the entire philosophy of the Gita. Sri Krishna establishes Himself as the ultimate Cause of all causes ('Sarvasya Prabhavaḥ'). The truly wise (Budhāḥ) do not remain dry theorists; understanding His supremacy, their hearts blossom with intense, loving devotional ecstasy (Bhāva).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् |
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् |
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: mat-cittāḥ—with minds absorbed in Me; mad-gata-prāṇāḥ—with lives surrendered unto Me; bodhayantaḥ parasparam—enlightening one another; kathayantaḥ ca mām—and speaking of My divine glories; nityam—always; tuṣyanti ca—they experience contentment; ramanti ca—and rejoice in spiritual bliss.
verses.translation: With their minds absorbed in Me, their lives surrendered unto Me, enlightening one another and constantly speaking of My divine glories, they remain ever contented and rejoice in divine bliss.
verses.meaning: The second verse of the Chatushloki Gita describes the sublime inner communion and community of pure devotees: Their consciousness is anchored in Krishna (Mac-cittā), their vital life-breath is offered to Him (Mad-gata-prāṇā), and they experience perpetual spiritual satisfaction (Tuṣyanti) and transcendental joy (Ramanti) by sharing Krishna-katha with fellow seekers.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् |
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् |
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam |
dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: teṣām—to them; satata-yuktānām—who are constantly devoted; bhajatām—worshiping; prīti-pūrvakam—with love and affection; dadāmi—I grant; buddhi-yogam tam—that yoga of spiritual intellect/wisdom; yena—by which; mām—unto Me; upayānti—they attain; te—they.
verses.translation: To those who are constantly devoted and who worship Me with loving devotion (Priti-purvakam), I bestow that yoga of spiritual intellect (Buddhi Yoga) by which they come unto Me.
verses.meaning: The third verse of the Chatushloki Gita reveals the divine mechanism of illumination: For the soul who surrenders with love, God Himself descends into the intellect as Buddhi Yoga—the intuitive, luminous discernment that guides the devotee straight into supreme divine communion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः |
नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः |
नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṃ tamaḥ |
nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: teṣām eva—for them indeed; anukampā-artham—out of divine compassion; aham—I; ajñāna-jam—born of ignorance; tamaḥ—darkness; nāśayāmi—destroy/dispel; ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ—dwelling within their hearts; jñāna-dīpena—with the lamp of wisdom; bhāsvatā—radiant/blazing.
verses.translation: Out of pure compassion for them, dwelling within their innermost heart, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the radiant lamp of spiritual wisdom (Jnana-dipa).
verses.meaning: The triumphant climax of the Chatushloki Gita: The Supreme Lord, seated as the Antaryamin (indwelling Paramatman) within the devotee's heart, personally ignites the blazing lamp of transcendental wisdom (Jnana-dipa), banishing every trace of spiritual darkness and worldly delusion.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् |
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् |
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |
puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; param brahma—the Supreme Brahman; param dhāma—the Supreme Abode; pavitram paramam—the Ultimate Purifier; bhavān—You are; puruṣam—the Supreme Person; śāśvatam—eternal; divyam—divine; ādi-devam—the Primeval Lord; ajam—unborn; vibhum—all-pervading.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: You are the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Abode, the Ultimate Purifier, the Eternal Divine Person, the Primeval Lord, the Unborn, and the All-Pervading!
verses.meaning: Overwhelmed by the Lord's Chatushloki revelation, Arjuna proclaims his complete realization of Sri Krishna's supreme divinity: Krishna is not merely a beloved friend or charioteer, but the Param Brahman, the eternal transcendental Person (Shashvata Purusha), and the all-pervading foundation of reality.
verses.purport: Overwhelmed by the Lord's Chatushloki revelation, Arjuna proclaims his complete realization of Sri Krishna's supreme divinity: Krishna is not merely a beloved friend or charioteer, but the Param Brahman, the eternal transcendental Person (Shashvata Purusha), and the all-pervading foundation of reality.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा |
असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा |
असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā |
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: āhuḥ—declare; tvām—You; ṛṣayaḥ sarve—all the great sages; deva-ṛṣiḥ nāradaḥ tathā—and the celestial sage Narada; asitaḥ—Asita; devalaḥ—Devala; vyāsaḥ—Vyasa; svayam—Yourself; ca eva—and surely; bravīṣi—You are declaring; me—unto me.
verses.translation: All the great sages proclaim this of You—the celestial sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and the great Vyasa; and now You Yourself are declaring it directly to me!
verses.meaning: Arjuna confirms that his realization is corroborated by the greatest spiritual authorities of Vedic history—Narada, Asita, Devala, and Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa—and is now directly validated by Sri Krishna's own words.
verses.purport: Arjuna confirms that his realization is corroborated by the greatest spiritual authorities of Vedic history—Narada, Asita, Devala, and Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa—and is now directly validated by Sri Krishna's own words.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव |
न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव |
न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
sarvametadṛtaṃ manye yanmāṃ vadasi keśava |
na hi te bhagavanvyaktiṃ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarvam—all; etat—this; ṛtam—truth; manye—I accept/believe; yat—what; mām—unto me; vadasi—You speak; keśava—O Keshava; na hi—neither indeed; te—Your; bhagavan—O Lord; vyaktim—manifestation/personality; viduḥ—comprehend; devāḥ—the gods; na dānavāḥ—nor the demons.
verses.translation: I accept as absolute truth all that You have spoken to me, O Keshava! Neither the celestial gods nor the demons, O Blessed Lord, comprehend Your divine personality.
verses.meaning: Arjuna exhibits total, unstinting faith (Ritammanye) in Sri Krishna's words. He acknowledges that without divine grace, neither heavenly beings nor powerful demons can penetrate the mystery of God's transcendental personhood.
verses.purport: Arjuna exhibits total, unstinting faith (Ritammanye) in Sri Krishna's words. He acknowledges that without divine grace, neither heavenly beings nor powerful demons can penetrate the mystery of God's transcendental personhood.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम |
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम |
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
svayamevātmanātmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama |
bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: svayam eva—You alone; ātmanā—by Yourself; ātmānam—Yourself; vettha—know; tvam—You; puruṣa-uttama—O Supreme Person; bhūta-bhāvana—O Origin of all beings; bhūta-īśa—O Lord of all creatures; deva-deva—O God of all gods; jagat-pate—O Master of the universe.
verses.translation: You alone know Yourself by Your own divine consciousness, O Supreme Person, Origin of all beings, Lord of all creatures, God of all gods, and Master of the universe!
verses.meaning: A beautiful crescendo of divine titles: Purushottama (Supreme Person), Bhuta-bhavana (Creator of beings), Bhutesha (Lord of beings), Deva-deva (God of gods), and Jagat-pati (Ruler of the cosmos). Only God has the infinite capacity to know Himself fully.
verses.purport: A beautiful crescendo of divine titles: Purushottama (Supreme Person), Bhuta-bhavana (Creator of beings), Bhutesha (Lord of beings), Deva-deva (God of gods), and Jagat-pati (Ruler of the cosmos). Only God has the infinite capacity to know Himself fully.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः |
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः |
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ |
yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṃstvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: vaktum arhasi—You should describe; aśeṣeṇa—without omission/in full; divyāḥ—divine; hi—indeed; ātma-vibhūtayaḥ—Your own divine opulences; yābhiḥ—by which; vibhūtibhiḥ—opulences; lokān imān—all these worlds; tvam—You; vyāpya—pervading; tiṣṭhasi—remain.
verses.translation: Please describe to me fully Your divine opulences (Vibhutis), by which You remain pervading all these worlds.
verses.meaning: Arjuna requests a comprehensive catalogue of Krishna's divine glories so that seekers can train their vision to see God everywhere in nature, art, wisdom, and life.
verses.purport: Arjuna requests a comprehensive catalogue of Krishna's divine glories so that seekers can train their vision to see God everywhere in nature, art, wisdom, and life.

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् |
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् |
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
kathaṃ vidyāmahaṃ yogiṃstvāṃ sadā paricintayan |
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: katham—how; vidyām aham—may I know; yogin—O Supreme Mystic; tvām—You; sadā—always; paricintayan—meditating upon; keṣu keṣu—in what various; ca—and; bhāveṣu—forms/aspects; cintyaḥ asi—are You to be meditated upon; bhagavan—O Lord; mayā—by me.
verses.translation: How may I know You, O Supreme Mystic, by constantly meditating on You? In what various aspects and forms are You to be contemplated by me, O Blessed Lord?
verses.meaning: Arjuna asks for practical guidance in Upasana (meditation): How can an ordinary mind keep its focus continually anchored in God when interacting with the multifaceted forms of creation?
verses.purport: Arjuna asks for practical guidance in Upasana (meditation): How can an ordinary mind keep its focus continually anchored in God when interacting with the multifaceted forms of creation?

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन |
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन |
भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana |
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: vistareṇa—in detail; ātmanaḥ—Your own; yogam—mystic power; vibhūtim ca—and divine opulence; janārdana—O Janardana; bhūyaḥ—again; kathaya—tell; tṛptiḥ—satiation; hi—truly; śṛṇvataḥ—hearing; na asti—there is not; me—for me; amṛtam—this nectar.
verses.translation: Tell me again in detail, O Janardana, of Your divine power and opulence! For I can never be satiated with drinking the nectar of Your immortal words.
verses.meaning: A touching expression of insatiable spiritual longing: The words of God are 'Amritam'—nectar that never gluts or bores the soul, but only deepens the seeker's thirst for divine union.
verses.purport: A touching expression of insatiable spiritual longing: The words of God are 'Amritam'—nectar that never gluts or bores the soul, but only deepens the seeker's thirst for divine union.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः |
प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः |
प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ |
prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: hanta—yes/verily; te—unto you; kathayiṣyāmi—I shall describe; divyāḥ—divine; hi—indeed; ātma-vibhūtayaḥ—My own opulences; prādhānyataḥ—the principal ones; kuru-śreṣṭha—O best of the Kurus; na asti—there is no; antaḥ—end; vistarasya—to the extent/expansion; me—of Mine.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Yes, I shall describe to you My divine opulences, but only the principal ones, O best of the Kurus, for there is no end to My cosmic manifestations.
verses.meaning: Because the infinite opulences of God are limitless, Sri Krishna agrees to highlight the foremost archetypes (Pradhanyatah) through which His divine presence shines most brilliantly in the cosmos.
verses.purport: Because the infinite opulences of God are limitless, Sri Krishna agrees to highlight the foremost archetypes (Pradhanyatah) through which His divine presence shines most brilliantly in the cosmos.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः |
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः |
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ |
ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: aham—I am; ātmā—the Self (Atman); guḍākeśa—O Gudakesha (conqueror of sleep/Arjuna); sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ—seated in the heart of all beings; aham—I am; ādiḥ ca—the beginning also; madhyam ca—and the middle; bhūtānām—of all beings; antaḥ—the end; eva ca—and also.
verses.translation: I am the Self (Atman), O Gudakesha, seated within the hearts of all living beings. I am the Beginning, the Middle, and the End of all creatures.
verses.meaning: The foundation of all Vibhutis: Before seeking God in outer objects, one must realize that Sri Krishna is the innermost Self (Atman) of every creature. He is the cosmic source of life's beginning, the sustaining presence during its lifespan, and the final haven of its dissolution.
verses.purport: The foundation of all Vibhutis: Before seeking God in outer objects, one must realize that Sri Krishna is the innermost Self (Atman) of every creature. He is the cosmic source of life's beginning, the sustaining presence during its lifespan, and the final haven of its dissolution.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् |
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् |
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān |
marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: ādityānām—of the twelve Adityas; aham—I am; viṣṇuḥ—Vishnu; jyotiṣām—of luminaries; raviḥ aṃśumān—the radiant Sun; marīciḥ—Marichi; marutām—of the wind-gods (Maruts); asmi—I am; nakṣatrāṇām—among stars/celestial bodies; aham—I am; śaśī—the Moon.
verses.translation: Among the twelve Adityas I am Vishnu; among radiant lights I am the radiant Sun; among the Maruts I am Marichi; and among the nocturnal celestial bodies I am the Moon.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna identifies Himself with the apex of celestial grandeur: Vishnu among solar deities, the life-giving Sun among luminaries, Marichi among wind gods, and the soothing Moon in the night sky.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna identifies Himself with the apex of celestial grandeur: Vishnu among solar deities, the life-giving Sun among luminaries, Marichi among wind gods, and the soothing Moon in the night sky.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः |
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः |
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: vedānām—of the Vedas; sāma-vedaḥ—the Sama Veda; asmi—I am; devānām—of the demigods; asmi—I am; vāsavaḥ—Indra; indriyāṇām—of the senses; manaḥ ca—the mind also; asmi—I am; bhūtānām—in living beings; asmi—I am; cetanā—living consciousness.
verses.translation: Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the celestial gods I am Indra (Vasava); among the senses I am the Mind (Manas); and in living beings I am Consciousness (Chetana).
verses.meaning: Krishna is the melodious Sama Veda, king of the gods Indra, the organizing central faculty of Mind among the senses, and above all, Chetana—the spark of sentient consciousness animating all living organisms.
verses.purport: Krishna is the melodious Sama Veda, king of the gods Indra, the organizing central faculty of Mind among the senses, and above all, Chetana—the spark of sentient consciousness animating all living organisms.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् |
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् |
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām |
vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: rudrāṇām—among the eleven Rudras; śaṅkaraḥ ca—Shankara (Shiva); asmi—I am; vitta-īśaḥ—Kubera (lord of treasures); yakṣa-rakṣasām—among Yakshas and Rakshasas; vasūnām—among the eight Vasus; pāvakaḥ ca—Pavaka (Fire/Agni); asmi—I am; meruḥ—Mount Meru; śikhariṇām—among peaked mountains; aham—I am.
verses.translation: Among the eleven Rudras I am Shankara (Shiva); among the Yakshas and Rakshasas I am Kubera (the lord of wealth); among the eight Vasus I am Pavaka (Fire); and among mountain peaks I am the golden Mount Meru.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna identifies with Shiva (Shankara, the auspicious transformer), Kubera (treasurer of cosmic wealth), Agni (sacred purifying fire), and Meru (the celestial axis mountain of Vedic cosmology).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna identifies with Shiva (Shankara, the auspicious transformer), Kubera (treasurer of cosmic wealth), Agni (sacred purifying fire), and Meru (the celestial axis mountain of Vedic cosmology).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् |
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् |
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: purodhasām—among priests; ca—and; mukhyam—the chief; mām—Me; viddhi—know; pārtha—O son of Pritha; bṛhaspatim—Brihaspati; senānīnām—among military commanders; aham—I am; skandaḥ—Skanda (Kartikeya); sarasām—among reservoirs of water; asmi—I am; sāgaraḥ—the ocean.
verses.translation: Know Me, O Partha, to be Brihaspati, the chief of celestial priests; among military generals I am Skanda (Kartikeya); and among bodies of water I am the boundless Ocean.
verses.meaning: Krishna is Brihaspati (guru of the gods), Skanda (invincible celestial commander), and Sagara (the majestic, fathomless ocean).
verses.purport: Krishna is Brihaspati (guru of the gods), Skanda (invincible celestial commander), and Sagara (the majestic, fathomless ocean).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् |
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् |
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram |
yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: mahā-ṛṣīṇām—among great sages; bhṛguḥ—Bhrigu; aham—I am; girām—among spoken words; asmi—I am; ekam akṣaram—the sacred single syllable (OM); yajñānām—among sacrifices; japa-yajñaḥ—the sacrifice of silent prayer/mantra chanting (Japa); asmi—I am; sthāvarāṇām—among immovable things; himālayaḥ—the Himalayas.
verses.translation: Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among vibrations of sound I am the sacred single syllable OM; among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of Japa (silent chanting); and among immovable things I am the majestic Himalayas.
verses.meaning: Japa Yajna—the silent, loving repetition of the holy name—is elevated as the supreme form of sacrifice, requiring no animal violence or external wealth. Krishna is also the sacred Pranava OM and the serene Himalayas.
verses.purport: Japa Yajna—the silent, loving repetition of the holy name—is elevated as the supreme form of sacrifice, requiring no animal violence or external wealth. Krishna is also the sacred Pranava OM and the serene Himalayas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः |
गन्धर्वानां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः |
गन्धर्वानां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
gandharvānāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: aśvatthaḥ—the sacred banyan/peepal tree; sarva-vṛkṣāṇām—among all trees; deva-ṛṣīṇām—among celestial sages; ca—and; nāradaḥ—Narada; gandharvānām—among Gandharvas (celestial musicians); citrarathaḥ—Chitraratha; siddhānām—among perfected beings; kapilaḥ muniḥ—Kapila Muni.
verses.translation: Among all trees I am the holy Ashvattha (sacred fig); among celestial sages I am Narada; among Gandharvas (celestial musicians) I am Chitraratha; and among perfected beings (Siddhas) I am sage Kapila.
verses.meaning: Krishna is the Ashvattha tree, the celestial troubadour Narada, Chitraratha, and Kapila Muni, the founder of the analytical Sankhya philosophy.
verses.purport: Krishna is the Ashvattha tree, the celestial troubadour Narada, Chitraratha, and Kapila Muni, the founder of the analytical Sankhya philosophy.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् |
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् |
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam |
airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: uccaiḥśravasam—Uchchaishravas; aśvānām—among horses; viddhi—know; mām—Me; amṛta-udbhavam—born of the nectar churning of the ocean; airāvatam—Airavata; gaja-indrāṇām—among noble elephants; narāṇām—among human beings; ca—and; nara-adhipam—the righteous king/monarch.
verses.translation: Among horses know Me to be Uchchaishravas, born from the churning of the ocean for nectar; among noble elephants I am Airavata; and among humans I am the Monarch.
verses.meaning: Krishna is Uchchaishravas (the divine steed of Indra), Airavata (the multi-tusked white elephant), and the righteous ruler who protects and serves society with wisdom.
verses.purport: Krishna is Uchchaishravas (the divine steed of Indra), Airavata (the multi-tusked white elephant), and the righteous ruler who protects and serves society with wisdom.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् |
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् |
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: āyudhānām—among weapons; aham—I am; vajram—the thunderbolt (Vajra); dhenūnām—among cows; asmi—I am; kāma-dhuk—Kamadhenu (the wish-yielding cow); prajanaḥ ca—and procreative desire; asmi—I am; kandarpaḥ—Kandarpa (Kamadeva); sarpāṇām—among single-headed serpents; asmi—I am; vāsukiḥ—Vasuki.
verses.translation: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt (Vajra); among cows I am Kamadhuk (the wish-yielding celestial cow); among procreative forces I am Kandarpa (the god of love); and among serpents I am Vasuki.
verses.meaning: Krishna is the thunderbolt fashioned from sage Dadhichi's bones, the wish-fulfilling Surabhi cow, the creative power of love for righteous procreation, and king Vasuki.
verses.purport: Krishna is the thunderbolt fashioned from sage Dadhichi's bones, the wish-fulfilling Surabhi cow, the creative power of love for righteous procreation, and king Vasuki.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् |
पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् || २९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् |
पितॄणामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham |
pitṝṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham || 29 ||
verses.word_meanings: anantaḥ ca—and Ananta (Shesha); asmi—I am; nāgānām—among many-headed celestial serpents; varuṇaḥ—Varuna; yādasām—among aquatic deities; aham—I am; pitṝṇām—among ancestors; aryamā—Aryama; ca asmi—and I am; yamaḥ—Yama (lord of death and justice); saṃyamatām—among dispensers of justice/law; aham—I am.
verses.translation: Among many-headed celestial serpents I am Ananta (Sheshanaga); among aquatic deities I am Varuna; among ancestral spirits I am Aryama; and among enforcers of law and justice I am Yama (the Lord of Dharma).
verses.meaning: Krishna is Ananta-Shesha (who cradles the cosmos), Varuna (sovereign of the cosmic waters), Aryama (leader of ancestors), and Yama (impartial dispenser of karmic justice).
verses.purport: Krishna is Ananta-Shesha (who cradles the cosmos), Varuna (sovereign of the cosmic waters), Aryama (leader of ancestors), and Yama (impartial dispenser of karmic justice).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् |
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् || ३० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् |
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham |
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro'haṃ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām || 30 ||
verses.word_meanings: prahlādaḥ ca—and Prahlada; asmi—I am; daityānām—among the Daityas (demons); kālaḥ—Time; kalayatām—among reckoners/subduers; aham—I am; mṛgāṇām—among wild beasts; ca—and; mṛga-indraḥ—the Lion (king of beasts); aham—I am; vainateyaḥ ca—and Garuda (son of Vinata); pakṣiṇām—among birds.
verses.translation: Among the Daityas I am the saintly Prahlada; among reckoners and conquerors I am Time (Kala); among beasts I am the majestic Lion (Mrigendra); and among winged birds I am Garuda (Vainateya).
verses.meaning: Krishna shines through Prahlada (the exemplar of pure devotion amidst demoniac adversity), inexorable Time (Kala) which measures and dissolves all worlds, the lion in the forest, and Garuda in the sky.
verses.purport: Krishna shines through Prahlada (the exemplar of pure devotion amidst demoniac adversity), inexorable Time (Kala) which measures and dissolves all worlds, the lion in the forest, and Garuda in the sky.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् |
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी || ३१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् |
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham |
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī || 31 ||
verses.word_meanings: pavanaḥ—the wind; pavatām—among purifiers; asmi—I am; rāmaḥ—Lord Rama; śastra-bhṛtām—among wielders of weapons; aham—I am; jhaṣāṇām—among aquatic creatures/fishes; makaraḥ ca—the Makara (shark/alligator); asmi—I am; srotasām—among flowing rivers; asmi—I am; jāhnavī—the sacred Ganges (daughter of Jahnu).
verses.translation: Among purifiers I am the Wind; among wielders of weapons I am Lord Rama; among aquatic creatures I am the Makara; and among sacred flowing rivers I am the holy Ganges (Jahnavi).
verses.meaning: Krishna is the purifying wind, the epitome of righteous chivalry Sri Ramachandra, the mighty aquatic Makara, and the sacred river Ganga whose waters purify the three worlds.
verses.purport: Krishna is the purifying wind, the epitome of righteous chivalry Sri Ramachandra, the mighty aquatic Makara, and the sacred river Ganga whose waters purify the three worlds.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन |
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् || ३२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन |
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṃ caivāhamarjuna |
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham || 32 ||
verses.word_meanings: sargāṇām—of creations; ādiḥ—the beginning; antaḥ ca—and the end; madhyam ca eva—and also the middle; aham—I am; arjuna—O Arjuna; adhyātma-vidyā—the science of the Supreme Self; vidyānām—among sciences/branches of knowledge; vādaḥ—Vada (logical debate for truth); pravadatām—of debates/discourses; aham—I am.
verses.translation: Of all creations I am the Beginning, the End, and the Middle, O Arjuna! Among all sciences I am the Science of the Supreme Self (Adhyatma Vidya); and in philosophical debate I am Vada—the quest for ultimate truth.
verses.meaning: Of all academic branches of knowledge, Krishna is Adhyatma Vidya (Self-knowledge), which bestows eternal liberation. In debate, He is Vada—the constructive dialogue aimed at discovering truth, distinct from contentious arguing (Jalpa) or cynical fault-finding (Vitanda).
verses.purport: Of all academic branches of knowledge, Krishna is Adhyatma Vidya (Self-knowledge), which bestows eternal liberation. In debate, He is Vada—the constructive dialogue aimed at discovering truth, distinct from contentious arguing (Jalpa) or cynical fault-finding (Vitanda).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च |
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुखः || ३३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च |
अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुखः || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca |
ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṃ viśvatomukhaḥ || 33 ||
verses.word_meanings: akṣarāṇām—of letters; a-kāraḥ—the letter 'A'; asmi—I am; dvandvaḥ—the dual compound (Dvandva); sāmāsikasya—of compound words; ca—and; aham eva—I alone am; akṣayaḥ kālaḥ—inexhaustible/eternal Time; dhātā—the Sustainer/Dispenser; aham—I am; viśvataḥ-mukhaḥ—facing in all directions.
verses.translation: Among letters of the alphabet I am the letter 'A' (Akara); among compound words I am the Dual compound (Dvandva); I alone am inexhaustible Time (Akshaya Kala); and I am the all-facing Dispenser and Sustainer of the cosmos.
verses.meaning: The letter 'A' is the root vowel without which no Sanskrit consonant can be vocalized. Krishna is also Akshaya Kala (limitless Time) and the universal Provider facing all directions.
verses.purport: The letter 'A' is the root vowel without which no Sanskrit consonant can be vocalized. Krishna is also Akshaya Kala (limitless Time) and the universal Provider facing all directions.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् |
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा || ३४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् |
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā || 34 ||
verses.word_meanings: mṛtyuḥ—death; sarva-haraḥ—all-devouring; ca—and; aham—I am; udbhavaḥ ca—and the origin/birth; bhaviṣyatām—of future things; kīrtiḥ—fame; śrīḥ—prosperity/beauty; vāk ca—and speech; nārīṇām—among feminine virtues; smṛtiḥ—memory; medhā—intellect; dhṛtiḥ—fortitude/patience; kṣamā—forgiveness.
verses.translation: I am all-devouring Death (Mrityu), and I am the source of all future beings to be born. Among feminine virtues I am Fame (Kirti), Prosperity (Shri), Eloquent Speech (Vak), Memory (Smriti), Intellect (Medha), Fortitude (Dhriti), and Forgiveness (Kshama).
verses.meaning: Krishna encompasses the great transition of Death (Sarva-hara Mrityu) and the continuous renewal of Life. He personifies the seven sublime divine feminine virtues in the human heart.
verses.purport: Krishna encompasses the great transition of Death (Sarva-hara Mrityu) and the continuous renewal of Life. He personifies the seven sublime divine feminine virtues in the human heart.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् |
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः || ३५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् |
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasāmaham |
māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ || 35 ||
verses.word_meanings: bṛhat-sāma—the Brihat-sama hymn; tathā—also; sāmnām—among the songs of the Sama Veda; gāyatrī—the sacred Gayatri mantra; chandasām—among poetic meters; aham—I am; māsānām—among the months; mārgaśīrṣaḥ—Margashirsha (Nov-Dec); aham—I am; ṛtūnām—among seasons; kusuma-ākaraḥ—flowering Spring (Vasant).
verses.translation: Among the hymns of the Sama Veda I am the Brihat-sama; among poetic meters I am the sacred Gayatri; among months I am Margashirsha (November–December); and among seasons I am flower-laden Spring (Kusumakara).
verses.meaning: Krishna is the majestic Brihat-sama, the Gayatri mantra (the mother of Vedic illumination), the spiritually auspicious month of Margashirsha, and Springtime in all its blossoming splendour.
verses.purport: Krishna is the majestic Brihat-sama, the Gayatri mantra (the mother of Vedic illumination), the spiritually auspicious month of Margashirsha, and Springtime in all its blossoming splendour.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् |
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् || ३६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् |
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् || ३६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dyūtaṃ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham |
jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatāmaham || 36 ||
verses.word_meanings: dyūtam—gambling; chalayatām—of the deceptive/crafty; asmi—I am; tejaḥ—the brilliance/splendor; tejasvinām—of the splendid; aham—I am; jayaḥ asmi—I am victory; vyavasāyaḥ asmi—I am determination/effort; sattvam—the goodness/purity; sattvavatām—of the virtuous; aham—I am.
verses.translation: I am the gambling of cheats, and the splendor of the splendid. I am Victory, I am Resolve, and I am the noble virtue of the virtuous.
verses.meaning: Even the cleverness of dice in worldly deception reflects the inescapable supremacy of divine destiny. Krishna is the glory of the brilliant, the triumph of the victorious, the determination of the resolute, and the pure goodness of noble souls.
verses.purport: Even the cleverness of dice in worldly deception reflects the inescapable supremacy of divine destiny. Krishna is the glory of the brilliant, the triumph of the victorious, the determination of the resolute, and the pure goodness of noble souls.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः |
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः || ३७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः |
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः || ३७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ || 37 ||
verses.word_meanings: vṛṣṇīnām—among the Vrishnis; vāsudevaḥ—Vasudeva (Krishna Himself); asmi—I am; pāṇḍavānām—among the Pandavas; dhanañjayaḥ—Dhananjaya (Arjuna); munīnām—among sages; api—also; aham—I am; vyāsaḥ—Vyasa; kavīnām—among seers/poets; uśanā kaviḥ—Ushana (Shukracharya).
verses.translation: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva (Krishna); among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya (Arjuna); among meditative sages I am Vyasa; and among visionary poets I am Ushana (Shukracharya).
verses.meaning: A poignant moment: Sri Krishna identifies Himself with Arjuna ('Pandavanam Dhananjayah'), illustrating the profound non-dual intimacy between the Supreme Lord and His dedicated friend and devotee.
verses.purport: A poignant moment: Sri Krishna identifies Himself with Arjuna ('Pandavanam Dhananjayah'), illustrating the profound non-dual intimacy between the Supreme Lord and His dedicated friend and devotee.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् |
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् || ३८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् |
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् || ३८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām |
maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatāmaham || 38 ||
verses.word_meanings: daṇḍaḥ—the sceptre of punishment/justice; damayatām—of rulers/lawgivers; asmi—I am; nītiḥ—statesmanship/righteous policy; asmi—I am; jigīṣatām—of those seeking victory; maunam—silence; ca eva—and surely; asmi—I am; guhyānām—of secret things; jñānam—wisdom; jñānavatām—of the wise; aham—I am.
verses.translation: I am the sceptre of authority among rulers; I am righteous statesmanship (Niti) among seekers of victory; I am Silence (Mauna) among secret mysteries; and I am the wisdom of the wise.
verses.meaning: Krishna is Danda (the rod of lawful governance that prevents anarchy), ethical statecraft (Niti), the sacred inward stillness of Silence (Mauna), and the illumination of enlightened sages.
verses.purport: Krishna is Danda (the rod of lawful governance that prevents anarchy), ethical statecraft (Niti), the sacred inward stillness of Silence (Mauna), and the illumination of enlightened sages.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन |
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् || ३९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन |
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् || ३९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tadahamarjuna |
na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram || 39 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat ca api—further whatever is; sarva-bhūtānām—of all beings; bījam—the generating seed; tat—that; aham—I am; arjuna—O Arjuna; na tat asti—there is nothing; vinā—without; yat syāt—which may exist; mayā—Me; bhūtam—being; cara-acaram—moving or unmoving.
verses.translation: Furthermore, O Arjuna, I am the generating seed of all existences. Nothing moving or unmoving can exist without Me!
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna is the primal seed (Bīja) of all life. Nothing in existence—from a blade of grass to a galaxy, from an atom to an archangel—can maintain its existence for even a single fraction of a second apart from God.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna is the primal seed (Bīja) of all life. Nothing in existence—from a blade of grass to a galaxy, from an atom to an archangel—can maintain its existence for even a single fraction of a second apart from God.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप |
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया || ४० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप |
एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया || ४० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
nānto'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa |
eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā || 40 ||
verses.word_meanings: na antaḥ asti—there is no limit/end; mama—to My; divyānām—divine; vibhūtīnām—opulences; parantapa—O scorcher of foes (Arjuna); eṣaḥ tu—this however; uddeśataḥ—by way of illustration/brief summary; proktaḥ—has been declared; vibhūteḥ vistaraḥ—the expanse of divine opulence; mayā—by Me.
verses.translation: There is no end to My divine opulences, O scorcher of foes! What I have spoken to you is merely a brief glimpse of the limitless extent of My manifestations.
verses.meaning: The Lord reminds Arjuna that words can never exhaust infinity. The catalogue given in Chapter 10 is only a modest illustrative spark (Uddeśataḥ) of the boundless ocean of divine majesty.
verses.purport: The Lord reminds Arjuna that words can never exhaust infinity. The catalogue given in Chapter 10 is only a modest illustrative spark (Uddeśataḥ) of the boundless ocean of divine majesty.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा |
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् || ४१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा |
तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् || ४१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā |
tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo'ṃśasambhavam || 41 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat yat—whatever; vibhūtimat—endowed with opulence/glory; sattvam—being/existence; śrīmat—endowed with beauty/prosperity; ūrjitam eva vā—or endowed with power/heroism; tat tat eva—all that indeed; avagaccha—understand; tvam—you; mama—My; tejaḥ-aṃśa-sambhavam—born of a mere spark of My divine splendor.
verses.translation: Whatever entity is glorious (Vibhūtimat), beautiful or prosperous (Śrīmat), or mighty and powerful (Ūrjitam)—know for certain that it springs from a mere spark of My divine splendor!
verses.meaning: The universal formula for recognizing God: Wherever one encounters extraordinary genius, breathtaking natural beauty, magnificent heroism, radiant goodness, or majestic power, one is witnessing an effulgent spark (Tejo-'ṁśa-sambhavam) of Sri Krishna's infinite divine brilliance.
verses.purport: The universal formula for recognizing God: Wherever one encounters extraordinary genius, breathtaking natural beauty, magnificent heroism, radiant goodness, or majestic power, one is witnessing an effulgent spark (Tejo-'ṁśa-sambhavam) of Sri Krishna's infinite divine brilliance.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन |
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् || ४२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन |
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् || ४२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
athavā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna |
viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat || 42 ||
verses.word_meanings: athavā—or else; bahunā etena—by this extensive detailed knowledge; kim jñātena—what need of knowing; tava—by you; arjuna—O Arjuna; viṣṭabhya—pervading and supporting; aham—I; idam—this; kṛtsnam—entire; eka-aṃśena—with a single fraction/part; sthitaḥ—remain situated; jagat—universe.
verses.translation: Or of what need is there, O Arjuna, for all this detailed knowledge? With a mere fraction (Ekamshena) of My being, I pervade and sustain this entire universe!
verses.meaning: The grand cosmic conclusion of Chapter 10: All the billions of galaxies, multiverses, celestial beings, and terrestrial kingdoms are sustained by a single fraction (Ekāṁśa) of Sri Krishna's transcendent Being. Having heard this revelation of infinite majesty, Arjuna will yearn in Chapter 11 to witness this Cosmic Form with his own eyes.
